correctness.rationale: For every spanning tree of K_{a,b}, the degree excess on the b-side equals a-1. The unique nonleaf skeleton is connected and acyclic; conditional on it, every other b-side vertex chooses an a-side neighbour independently and uniformly. For two trees, at most 2(a-1) b-side vertices occur in either skeleton, so conditioning extracts an independent Bin(b-2a+2,1/a) factor with nonnegative residual coefficients. Since the total overlap degree is at most a+b-1, the residual degree is at most 3(a-1). For a=3, classifying the degree-excess partitions 2 and 1+1 gives the I/II skeleton enumeration; an exhaustive eight-relation skeleton-pair table, with exact conditional probabilities, yields the displayed Q_n polynomial and ordered disjoint pair count. Independent exact tree-pair enumeration agrees for n=4,5 (4,287,249 ordered pairs), and exact rational polynomial identities check n=4..40. These finite checks are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest directly relevant source (Bóna, Burghart and Wagner, arXiv:2501.18570v4, Section 5) describes approximately binomial overlap for fixed small bipartition size but does not give the exact independent binomial factor, a three-by-n correction polynomial or the zero-overlap enumeration. Earlier complete-bipartite and multipartite forest-extension identities count completions of a fixed forest, not the full overlap law of two independent trees. A known two-row overlap formula does not determine the three-row correction or its tree-packing corollary. Related tree-packing existence bounds do not give the number of ordered tree pairs. The exact statement was not found in the accessed literature comparisons; historical priority may still be revised.
residual_risks: Older exact pair-overlap formulas may exist under alternative tree-packing, reliability or matrix-tree terminology.
General forest-extension identities could support a different derivation of the same finite polynomial after significant additional enumeration.

value.rationale: The fixed-small-side bipartite regime was explicitly identified as non-Poisson in recent research, yet the approximation leaves finite distribution, small-n corrections and the zero-overlap probability undetermined. Theorem 1 supplies a structurally motivated independent binomial factor for all fixed small-side sizes, and Theorem 2 determines every coefficient for the first nontrivial three-row family. The zero-overlap specialization independently counts an infinite family of ordered edge-disjoint tree pairs, a natural exact tree-packing invariant; the law and correction polynomial are not isolated low-order numerics.
